name: Mercury
short_description: A small, heavily cratered world of rock and iron, baked by day and frozen by night with almost no atmosphere to soften the extremes.

interior.name: Crust
interior.description: A thin, heavily cratered silicate shell.

interior.name: Mantle
interior.description: A relatively thin rocky mantle surrounding the core.

interior.name: Core
interior.description: An unusually large iron core, thought to make up roughly 85% of the planet's radius.

highlights: Heavily cratered surface shaped by billions of years of impacts
Unusually large iron core relative to its size
Extremely thin exosphere offers almost no insulation
Extreme temperature swings between day and night
A solar day (sunrise to sunrise) lasts about 176 Earth days due to its slow spin and fast orbit
The Caloris Basin is one of the largest impact craters in the Solar System
Water ice has been detected in permanently shadowed polar craters
facts: Mercury has the most eccentric orbit of any planet in the Solar System.
Despite being closest to the Sun, Mercury is not the hottest planet — Venus is.
A year on Mercury (88 Earth days) is shorter than its solar day.

name: Venus
short_description: A cloud-shrouded world with a crushing, scorching atmosphere driven by a runaway greenhouse effect — the hottest planet in the Solar System.

atmosphere.summary: Thick carbon dioxide atmosphere with sulfuric acid clouds

interior.name: Crust
interior.description: A basaltic volcanic surface with tens of thousands of volcanoes.

interior.name: Mantle
interior.description: A thick silicate mantle, likely convecting slowly beneath the crust.

interior.name: Core
interior.description: A metallic iron-nickel core, likely partly molten.

highlights: Runaway greenhouse effect traps heat beneath a thick CO2 atmosphere
Clouds of sulfuric acid droplets reflect sunlight, making Venus the brightest planet in our sky
Rotates in retrograde (opposite most planets) and extremely slowly
A day on Venus (243 Earth days) is longer than its year (224.7 Earth days)
Surface shows evidence of extensive past volcanic activity
Hotter than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun, due to its insulating atmosphere
facts: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
Venus rotates in the opposite direction to most planets, a trait called retrograde rotation.
Venus's surface pressure is similar to being about 900 meters underwater on Earth.

name: Earth
short_description: Our home — the only known world with liquid water oceans, a breathable atmosphere, and life, shaped by plate tectonics and a protective magnetic field.

interior.name: Crust
interior.description: A thin rocky outer layer, thinnest under the oceans and thickest under mountain ranges.

interior.name: Mantle
interior.description: A thick layer of hot, slowly flowing rock that drives plate tectonics.

interior.name: Outer Core
interior.description: Liquid iron and nickel whose motion generates Earth's protective magnetic field.

interior.name: Inner Core
interior.description: A solid sphere of iron and nickel under immense pressure at the planet's center.

highlights: About 71% of the surface is covered by liquid water oceans
A global magnetic field deflects harmful solar wind and cosmic radiation
Plate tectonics continuously reshape the surface over geologic time
A rich biosphere makes Earth the only known world with life
Axial tilt of 23.4° produces the seasons
Charged particles interacting with the magnetic field create the aurora
facts: Earth is the only known planet with liquid water stable on its surface.
Earth's magnetic field is generated by the churning liquid outer core.
Earth's atmosphere protects the surface from most meteoroids, which burn up as they fall.

name: Mars
short_description: The 'Red Planet' — a cold desert world with the largest volcano and canyon in the Solar System, and strong evidence of a wetter ancient past.

interior.name: Crust
interior.description: A rocky, iron-oxide rich crust that gives Mars its reddish color.

interior.name: Mantle
interior.description: A silicate mantle, thicker relative to the planet's size than Earth's.

interior.name: Core
interior.description: A dense iron-rich core, likely partly liquid.

highlights: Olympus Mons is the tallest known volcano in the Solar System
Valles Marineris is a canyon system stretching thousands of kilometers
Polar ice caps made of water ice and frozen carbon dioxide grow and shrink with the seasons
Dry riverbeds and mineral evidence point to liquid water in the ancient past
Planet-wide dust storms can occasionally engulf the entire globe
The thin atmosphere provides little protection from radiation and heat loss
facts: Mars is home to Olympus Mons, roughly three times the height of Mount Everest.
Evidence suggests rivers, lakes, and possibly oceans existed on Mars billions of years ago.
A Martian year lasts almost twice as long as an Earth year.

name: Jupiter
short_description: The largest planet in the Solar System, a churning giant of hydrogen and helium famous for its Great Red Spot and a sprawling family of moons.

atmosphere.pressure: Increases steeply with depth; no solid surface

interior.name: Upper Atmosphere
interior.description: Colorful bands of ammonia clouds driven by rapid rotation.

interior.name: Molecular Hydrogen Layer
interior.description: A deep layer where hydrogen behaves as a gas, then a liquid, as pressure increases.

interior.name: Metallic Hydrogen Layer
interior.description: Under extreme pressure, hydrogen becomes electrically conductive, generating Jupiter's powerful magnetic field.

interior.name: Core (conceptual)
interior.description: A dense central region of heavier elements, possibly partly dissolved into the surrounding layers.

highlights: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm larger than Earth that has raged for centuries
Jupiter has the strongest planetary magnetic field in the Solar System
Rapid rotation (under 10 hours) creates Jupiter's banded cloud pattern
Jupiter is more massive than all other planets combined
Known moons number over 90, including four large Galilean moons
facts: Jupiter is so massive that its barycenter with the Sun lies just outside the Sun's surface.
The Great Red Spot has been observed for at least 150 years, possibly much longer.
Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet in the Solar System.

name: Saturn
short_description: Famous for its brilliant ring system, Saturn is a vast, low-density gas giant with dozens of moons, including the hazy, lake-studded Titan.

atmosphere.pressure: Increases steeply with depth; no solid surface

interior.name: Upper Atmosphere
interior.description: Pale bands of ammonia-ice clouds, calmer in appearance than Jupiter's.

interior.name: Molecular Hydrogen Layer
interior.description: A deep gaseous-to-liquid hydrogen layer.

interior.name: Metallic Hydrogen Layer
interior.description: Compressed conductive hydrogen that helps generate Saturn's magnetic field.

interior.name: Core (conceptual)
interior.description: A dense central region of rock, ice, and metal.

highlights: The ring system is made of countless particles of ice and rock, from dust-sized to house-sized
The Cassini Division is a prominent gap separating major ring sections
Saturn is the least dense planet — it would float in a large enough tub of water
A striking hexagonal jet-stream pattern swirls at Saturn's north pole
Titan, its largest moon, has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane
facts: Saturn's rings span hundreds of thousands of kilometers but are remarkably thin.
Saturn's density is lower than water.
Titan is the only moon in the Solar System known to have a substantial atmosphere.

name: Uranus
short_description: A pale cyan ice giant tipped almost completely on its side, giving it the most extreme seasons of any planet in the Solar System.

atmosphere.pressure: Increases with depth; no solid surface

interior.name: Upper Atmosphere
interior.description: A hazy, relatively featureless blue-green atmosphere colored by methane absorbing red light.

interior.name: Icy Mantle
interior.description: A dense fluid of water, ammonia, and methane 'ices' surrounding the core.

interior.name: Core (conceptual)
interior.description: A small rocky core relative to the planet's overall size.

highlights: Axial tilt of about 98° means Uranus essentially rotates on its side
Extreme seasons last roughly 20 years each due to the tilt and long orbit
Methane in the upper atmosphere absorbs red light, producing a cyan-blue color
Faint, narrow rings were discovered in 1977
Coldest planetary atmosphere in the Solar System has been recorded here
facts: Uranus rotates almost on its side, likely due to an ancient massive collision.
Uranus was the first planet discovered with a telescope, by William Herschel in 1781.
A season on Uranus lasts about 21 Earth years.

name: Neptune
short_description: The most distant major planet — a deep blue, dynamic ice giant known for the fastest winds recorded in the Solar System.

atmosphere.pressure: Increases with depth; no solid surface

interior.name: Upper Atmosphere
interior.description: A vivid blue, dynamic atmosphere with the fastest winds measured on any planet.

interior.name: Icy Mantle
interior.description: A hot, dense fluid of water, ammonia, and methane surrounding the core.

interior.name: Core (conceptual)
interior.description: A small rocky core relative to the planet's overall size.

highlights: Winds can exceed 2,000 km/h, the fastest recorded in the Solar System
Dark storm systems, such as the historic Great Dark Spot, appear and fade over time
Neptune radiates more heat than it receives from the distant Sun
Discovered in 1846 through mathematical prediction before it was directly observed
Triton, its largest moon, orbits backward and is likely a captured Kuiper Belt object
facts: Neptune was the first planet located through mathematical prediction rather than direct observation.
Neptune has the strongest sustained winds of any planet in the Solar System.
Neptune takes about 165 Earth years to complete one orbit of the Sun.
